text.text: When something happens to a body part or personal item belonging to someone, Spanish uses

plus a definite article instead of a possessive adjective: «le robaron la cartera» (they stole his/her wallet), rather than «robaron su cartera». With a pronominal verb of accidental events (caerse, romperse), the verb's own se comes first: «se le cayó el vaso a Juan» (Juan dropped the glass).

edits.replace: When the subject is a thing or an activity — by far the most common case — the verb takes only two forms in the present: third-person singular (when the subject is singular or an infinitive) and third-person plural (when the subject is plural).
